From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Follow-up: Marketplace private offer & unit-price mapping (post-call recap)

Hi Evan —

Thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and the open items so we can move to a marketplace private offer: 

1) Volumes: you mentioned initial pilot traffic of ~100M tokens/month with potential to grow to 200–250M tokens/month within 6–9 months. Please correct if I have that wrong.
2) Budget / target unit economics: you said procurement is aiming for a target net price in the ballpark of $120–$150 per 1M tokens.
3) Procurement preference: BrightCart prefers to purchase via AWS Marketplace Private Offer (single PO, easier audit).
4) Next asks from our side: to map Redwood list price -> AWS private offer net price we need a firm target net $/1M and an expected monthly token range so we can propose the SKU and list price that nets to your target after marketplace fees and partner margins.

I've attached a quick token estimate workbook you can fill with expected monthly ranges by environment (dev/stage/prod) — that will help us produce a clean private-offer mapping.

Attachments: BrightCart_token_estimates.xlsx

Proposed next steps: 
- Evan / procurement: confirm the expected monthly token range for the pilot and target net $/1M tokens (or acceptable range).
- Marissa + Rafael (partners) + Vivek (pricing): we'll produce a draft private-offer mapping (list price per 1M tokens on AWS/GCP/Azure) and routing options (hosted vs dedicated) for your review.

If it's easier, happy to set a 20-minute follow-up to align with procurement and your AWS Marketplace rep — let me know availability.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Marketplace private offer & unit-price mapping — BrightCart (draft mapping + next steps)

Team — quick draft back after running the numbers for AWS Private Offer. High level assumptions: 
- Target net to customer: $130 per 1M tokens (midpoint of the $120–$150 range).
- AWS Marketplace fee assumption: ~12% (typical for private offers; confirm with AM).
- Redwood target margin/discount layer for marketplace commit (what we can offer while protecting unit economics): 10–18% depending on commit & term.

Draft mapping (AWS Private Offer):
- Nominal list price suggestion: $150 per 1M tokens. After AWS ~12% fee (~$18) and a 10% partner discount (~$15) net ~ $117 — this is slightly below the $120 floor.
- To hit $130 net, list price needs to be roughly $170 per 1M tokens (170 - 12%*170 (~20.4) - 10% discount (~17) => ~132.6 net).

Recommendation: propose two tiers on the private offer:
1) Pilot (100M/mo): list price $170 per 1M tokens — nets ~ $131.
2) Commit tier (200M+): list price $150 per 1M tokens with a committed-term rebate (annual) or a higher reserved capacity discount — nets ~ $117 but with a volume rebate to get to target economics across term.

Notes / next steps:
- We should validate exact AWS fee percentage with the AWS AM (I can loop them in once Marissa approves the draft).
- For GCP/Azure marketplace mapping the fee structures differ — will need separate mapping.
- Operational constraints: if BrightCart needs dedicated reserved capacity to meet latency SLOs, that affects unit cost; we should include a section that shows hosted vs dedicated CPU/GPU economics per 1M tokens so procurement understands trade-offs.
- Attachments: AWS_private_offer_template.pdf (filled draft will be prepared).

I'll prepare a 1-page that shows list-price => marketplace-fee => partner-discount => net per 1M tokens, with an example calculation for 100M and 250M monthly volumes. Happy to jump on a 20–30 minute call with BrightCart + AWS AM to finalize.

Rafael Mendes
Partner Programs | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com
